window_frame.note: Background Setting and Showcase preserve layered black/gray 4Dwm frames, double bevel, corners, and directional relief.

title_bar.note: Showcase preserves the compact gray key band, italic title, left window-menu plate, and right caption plates.

window_buttons.note: Showcase's complete 690×32 key-title construction is reconstructed pixel-for-pixel, including the shared 4Dwm dither phase, leading window-menu plate, trailing minimize/maximize plates, stepped frame, and native one-bit caption face.

toolbar.note: Showcase preserves dense SGI menu/tool rows, rulers, small arrow plates, and hard separators.

buttons.note: Background Setting preserves the Motif-like raised command row with crisp highlight/shadow construction.

choice_controls.note: Background Setting preserves a selected list, colour well, thumb, and arrow controls in one native panel.

fields.note: The Showcase file browser preserves a focused pink text well with black inner rule, deep gray/white relief, insertion caret, and adjacent action buttons.

menus.note: The full desktop preserves Toolchest as a persistent compact menu palette with row rules and hard relief.

popovers.note: SGI's own Indigo Magic User Interface Guidelines (007-2167-001, 1994) define six kinds of online help and no hover surface at all: context-sensitive help is entered through a Help menu's Click for Help item or Shift-F1, the pointer becomes a question mark, and the answer opens in a separate SGI Help Viewer window (printed page 79, Figure 4-3). Threading should answer 'what is this' in a panel, not a floating tip.

scrollbars.note: Background Setting's complete 16×172 vertical scroller is reconstructed pixel-for-pixel: asymmetric 20/18px arrows, 90px page region, 44px gripped thumb, rails, seams, and seven-tone indexed relief.

lists_tables.note: Background Setting and Icon Catalog preserve dense rows, icon grids, hierarchy, selection, and scroller seating.

progress.note: SGI's own guidelines prescribe the Indigo Magic scale as the percent-done indicator and print it twice: Figure 10-6 gives a whole Working dialog (frame, italic Progress caption, framed message well, value label, inset trough with the scale's slanted leading edge, and a ringed default Cancel), Figure 9-7 gives the bare scale. Both figures are printed in grayscale, so construction and proportion are measurable from them but colour is not; take colour from the native Background Setting crops.

alerts_toasts.note: The native logout confirmation preserves the compact framed panel, bright green question icon, message well, button spacing, and return-key marker. Production keeps the icon-free Workbench requester separate and restores this IRIX question field with its source green role.

typography.note: The 1280x1024 desktop and focused panels preserve SGI screen fonts, italic caption text, and compact Motif metrics.

icons.note: Icon Catalog and Showcase preserve the SGI desktop/tool icon family at native scale.

tolerance.method: Full-crop native-1x RGB RMSE after exact 690×32 size validation. All 22,080 pixels are identical: the shared four-colour 4Dwm frame/dither construction, three caption plates, all rails and joins, and the native one-bit Showcase title rendered from the openly licensed X.Org Adobe Helvetica Bold Oblique screen face with six measured IRIX glyph deltas.

reproductions.note: Production WindowTitleBandView reconstructs the corrected tight 690×32 Showcase title assembly pixel-for-pixel. The former 691px crop included one blue desktop column beyond the native window; the exact target preserves only the stepped frame, shared dither, three live semantic button regions, and period bitmap caption.

tolerance.method: Full-crop native-1x RGB RMSE after exact 16×172 size validation, plus native-pixel review of the asymmetric 20px and 18px line buttons, 90px page region, 44px thumb with three grip seams, rails, and seven-colour indexed relief.

reproductions.note: Production ThemedScroller renders the tight 16×172 Background Setting control extraction pixel-for-pixel. Every one of its 2,752 pixels is identical; the wider crop remains supporting context for panel seating.
